Barratt of Ealing was an easy winner in 43.17, followed by Olney 44.13, and Ingles another minute back, third Peter Bagnall ran well to be 4th in 45.42, but he had no backing from the rest who included Short 9th, Gebbett 12th, Abbott 13th, L. Bishop 14th, Collis 17th.
The "B" Team slowly progressed after their bad start and thanks to good runs by Collis, Len Bishop and Hitchcock, pulled up to 14th position. 30 teams finished.

Meanwhile Collis had run very well to pull up the "B" Team from 17th to 10th position and Carter had maintained the Vets' position. Bagnall ran well to give us a lead of 19 seconds whilst Charlie Smart was pulling the Vets' team up a few places and a lot of time.
The journey through Redhill to the "Prince Albert" was Colin Collis's leg. He ran very well to do the fourth fastest time of the day and take us up one place to fifth.

Before the race we knew that Colin Collis and Eric Gebbett had strong claims on the Tommy Lalande Trophy, awarded to the first newcomer to finish and that our team could at least be placed in the Southern Championship, but at the final reckoning we had first and second places in the Lalande Trophy,…

The Southern 20 Miles Road Race was held on 5th May in conjunction with the Essex County Race at Brentwood, and our team was weakened by the absence of Colin Collis and Geoff Pearson, but we felt fairly confident of a place.

As a complete result did not appear in the last issue of the magazine, we take the liberty of supplying the missing details. In addition to Collis, Gebbett and Plummer whose positions and times were given, the following members completed the course:- 44th.

The race seemed to resolve itself quite rapidly into two fierce battles, between O'Gorman, Brown, Keily, Hicks, Lambert and Haslam on the one hand and a close bunch of a dozen, including our own trio, Colin Collis, Eric Gebbett and Len Bishop on the other.
At 5 miles Jack Brown had "lost" the field and looked set for another easy win, Colin Collis followed in 5th position from Chas Walker, Dave Baulch, Eric Gebbett and Len Bishop.

8th Colin Collis Good running in fifteen and twenty mile races is not the qualification for taking the second longest leg of this event against opposition such as Ken Norris, Mick Firth and Johnny Nichols, all of whom are seasoned international performers.
A number of those entered could not attend and we eventually started four teams of which three finished. The runners on the first stage were Walker(A), Collis(D), L.
